thread:
incident-bot: SEV-2 | ACME VPC gateway: increased websocket disconnects and streaming timeouts detected across region eu-west-1. Alerting on high 503s + client disconnects. auto-page: @eng-runtime-pager @sre-lina

ashley_w: paging in — logs show spikes in `ws_close` and `upstream_timeout`. ACME reports degraded streaming in their app (chat/video captions). They're on a Dedicated VPC gateway and using persistent websockets.

maria_s: I'm oncall. joining. any customer-impact estimate?

ivan_k: seeing many `502/503` from envoy layer -> upstream shard 12 (dedicated-pool-acme-12). Connection reset by peer and `context deadline exceeded` in runtime logs.

ashley_w: confirmed from ACME slack: users see "connection lost, retrying" and some messages dropped. Severity: customer-visible, partial (some connections succeed).

incident-bot: ACME ticket #ACME-512 created, severity assigned: P1-customer-impact. Notifying account execs.

josh_a: I just pinged the ACME SRE to say we're investigating. They asked if this is on our side or theirs — any quick mitigation before I reply?

ivan_k: short term: recommend toggling their client to exponential backoff and fall back to polling. But we need an infra mitigation ASAP. Possible causes: keepalive/idle timeout mismatch on customer LB -> our gateway, or overloaded dedicated pool node hitting FD limits.

eng-runtime-pager: I'm taking lead for runtime side. Checking GPU host and libuv connection counts.

sre-lina: I'll check LB and node-level metrics. If FD exhaustion, we can drain and rotate the node and increase `worker_connections` in our envoy config for the dedicated pool.

maria_s: action list for now: 1) increase gateway websocket idle timeout to 120s (was 60s) for acme routes 2) set temporary frontend retry attempts=2 3) route new connections away from shard-12 to shard-9/10 by updating routing weight

ivan_k: running quick grep of logs — relevant snippet:
```
2026-03-15T11:03:21Z runtime[shard-12]: ws_read error: read tcp 10.4.5.12:443: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T11:03:21Z envoy[shard-12]: upstream response timeout after 30s
2026-03-15T11:03:21Z runtime[shard-12]: kv-cache miss spike, increased latency
```

ashley_w: kv-cache miss spike could exacerbate latency and push some streaming requests over timeouts. Can we enable prefix cache warm-up for ACME for a few minutes?

eng-runtime-pager: we can push a temp config to warm some prefixes, but it's not instantaneous. Prioritize routing off the shard. I'll prepare a canary route change.

sre-lina: ops note: node-12 has 92% inode usage and ephemeral filedescriptors at ~85%. I'm going to cordon and drain after we shift traffic.

maria_s: @josh_a please tell ACME: we're seeing streaming timeouts from our VPC gateway, we've identified a noisy shard and are doing a rolling traffic shift plus increasing websocket idle timeout. We'll provide an ETA 30 min.

josh_a: sending: "We see client disconnects; shifting traffic and applying timeout tweaks. Short service disruption possible during mitigation. ETA 30-45m, will update." :thumbsup:

ivan_k: implementing routing change now — moving 40% traffic off shard-12 to shard-9 and shard-10. Command: `redwood route update --pool acme-dedicated --shard shard-12 --weight 0.6 --target shard-9,shard-10`

eng-runtime-pager: change applied. Monitoring connections.

incident-bot: automation: routing weight change executed, health-checks green.

sre-lina: starting drain of node-12. Draining connections may take ~2-5m for persistent websockets.

maria_s: also enabling `acme-vpc:streaming.disable_transfer_encoding = true` as a test to reduce proxy overhead. Will revert if no effect.

ivan_k: after drain started, I see 503 rate drop from 18% -> 6% over 3 minutes. Good signal.

ashley_w: kv-cache warms in progress — hit rate improved from 20% -> 65% on hot prefixes. Latency percentiles improving.

josh_a: ACME SRE replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted. If you need a mitigation on our side, we can temporarily disable streaming client feature flag."

maria_s: we should avoid asking ACME to disable streaming unless absolutely necessary. Plan B: if 503s don't decrease to <1%, ask them to flip client to polling. For now continue monitoring.

eng-runtime-pager: telemetry shows 99th latency down from 4.1s -> 1.2s for affected routes. 503s trending down.

sre-lina: node-12 drained successfully; removing from rotation. Will reprovision a fresh instance with increased ulimit and updated envoy config.

maria_s: prepare post-incident actions: 1) permanent increase of envoy `upstream_timeout` for vpc gateways from 30s -> 60s; 2) add FD pressure alert for dedicated pools; 3) guidance doc for customers about retry/backoff defaults for streaming clients; 4) add ability in console to toggle streaming fallback to polling per-tenant.

ivan_k: note: warm-up tooling should be automated for dedicated pools on rollout. I'll file a ticket.

incident-bot: SEV-2 -> mitigated. Monitoring phase.

josh_a: messaging update to ACME: "We routed traffic away from the noisy node, repaired the node configuration and increased websocket timeouts. We're continuing to monitor and will share a full RCA and remediation plan within 24h."

ashley_w: recording action items and owners: `ENG-RUNTIME` ivan_k -> automate warm-up + routing playbook; `SRE` lina -> increase default ulimit and update envoy config; `PRODUCT` maria_s -> console toggle for streaming fallback; `ACCOUNT` josh_a -> customer comms and postmortem timeline.

sre-lina: I'll follow up with PR to bump `worker_connections` and `ulimit` and schedule a canary for next maintenance window.

eng-runtime-pager: handing off to monitoring watch for 60m. If any regression, re-page.

maria_s: thanks all, closing active mitigation. We'll move to RCA thread and include logs and timeline.

josh_a: thanks team — I'll sync with ACME in 15m and confirm they see improvement. :white_check_mark:
